steps.instruction: Place the battery on the breadboard with positive and negative on separate power rails.
Connect the resistor from the positive rail to a row on the breadboard.
Connect the LED anode (longer leg) to the resistor, cathode to the negative rail.
Connect the switch in series between the LED cathode and negative rail.
Close the switch to complete the circuit and light the LED.
Use the multimeter to measure voltage across the LED.

rules.feedback: Battery placed on power rails. Positive on red rail, negative on blue rail.
Resistor connected from positive rail to breadboard row.
LED connected: anode to resistor, cathode toward negative rail.
Switch connected in series with the LED cathode.
Switch closed! Current flows and the LED lights up.
Multimeter reads the forward voltage drop across the LED (~2V).

outcomes.title: Series circuit complete
outcomes.description: The series circuit is working: battery → resistor → LED → switch → battery. Current flows through all components in one path.

safeFailure.message: The circuit didn't work as expected.
safeFailure.guidance: Check each connection. In a series circuit, all components must be connected in a single loop.

narration.text: Place the battery across the power rails. The positive terminal goes to the red rail, negative to the blue rail.
Connect a wire from the positive rail to a breadboard row, then place the resistor in that row.
Connect the LED's longer leg (anode) to the other end of the resistor. The shorter leg (cathode) goes toward the negative rail.
Insert the switch between the LED cathode and the negative rail. This will let you turn the circuit on and off.
Close the switch. The circuit is now complete — current flows and the LED lights!
Measure the voltage across the LED with the multimeter. You should see about 2 volts for a red LED.
